newsitem.title: USA: Group backs off effort to control Raymond.
newsitem.headline: Group backs off effort to control Raymond.

text.p: A New York-based group of investment partnerships said Wednesday that is reconsidering its plan to seize control of the Raymond Corp. board after the company agreed to consider proposals for a sale or merger.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Comission, the group, which includes Bedford Falls Investors L.P. and Metropolitan Capital Advisors Inc., said it agreed with the company to push its annual meeting back to June 2 from May 3.

The group's agreement, contained in a March 24 letter to the company, would allow time for a special committee of Raymond Corp. directors to solicit and evaluate proposals for a sale or merger of the company based on information on potential acquirers provided by the group, it said.

The group holds 7.51 percent of the company's common stock but has deals with other holders, including George Raymond, a company director, and members of his family, that give it voting control of 24.27 percent.

It said its agreement to postpone the annual meeting and defer a decision on seeking control of the board was based on Raymond's assurances that "a program to achieve the maximization of shareholder value has been actively undertaken."

Its decision on whether to propose increasing the board's size to 13 from 10 and to run candidates for six board vacancies may not be made until the end of April and would be affected by the Raymond board committee's progress in considering its proposals, it said.

Raymond, a Greene, N.Y., supplier of equipment used in transportation, storage and selection of products in manufacturing warehousing, said earlier this month that it had adopted a shareholder rights plan and had retained Lehman Brothers to advise it on strategic alternatives.
The Metropolitan Group includes its executive officers Jeffrey Shwarz and Karen Finerman.
